findings.title: Resident process loses S3 after an in-place package upgrade
findings.why_it_matters: If the packaged private module is replaced by a newer build while the resident executable is still running and has not yet loaded S3, the old executable rejects its new build identity on first network use. The failure is cached for that resident lifetime. The error tells the user to reinstall, while restarting the resident executable is the necessary recovery after that upgrade. This is a recovery-guidance concern; rejecting an incompatible private ABI and preserving local work are required behavior. The trigger is supported by the resident/autostart and upgrade design, but its incidence was not measured in this review.
findings.validation_reason: If an in-place upgrade replaces the installed S3 module before the old resident first loads it, the new exact-build check caches rejection for that resident (S3Module.cpp:55–64; S3Provider.cpp:33,74–79), but the externally returned message at S3Module.cpp:24 recommends only reinstalling rather than restarting into the matching executable, an ordering permitted by CMakeLists.txt:75–105 and the retained resident at main.cpp:31–34,71–74; incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Exercise same-version incompatible module rejection
findings.why_it_matters: A stale module from another application build can share contract version 1 while carrying a different private C++/Qt ABI or destructive transport contract. Both incompatible-module tests reject their fixture at the version check, so removing the build-identity or transport guard would leave those tests passing. This leaves the new same-build boundary without a regression test for the realistic partial-upgrade case; this is a coverage defect, not evidence that the current guards are wrong.
findings.validation_reason: A matching-version module with a wrong build identity or opposite safeDeleteTransport is not exercised: the sole new incompatible factory uses version+1 (test_s3_module.cpp:5), both direct/deployed failure cases reuse it (:94–116; CMakeLists.txt:215–222), and S3Module.cpp:61–64 short-circuits before those guards, while the scoped test search and test_sdk_contract.cpp:18–89 show lifecycle/header checks rather than alternate module fixtures, so removing either guard would leave these negative tests passing; no mutation run was performed.
